So, uh Bernard, the rookie, knows what it is with Rodgers and he's fixing to uh attach it the hip and I'd love to see that relationship, even though rookies don't necessarily flower, especially in the early uh part of the season, I'd love to see that blossom. >> Yeah, I mean, these guys, when you think of J'Mar, uh you know, he is detailed. He is a hard worker. And the you know, if rookies and Rodgers, as I mentioned, don't always mesh well, right? These young guys sometimes don't get the full picture. But I think he does. He's a guy that just kind of gets it. I mean, he didn't go, you know, up to Wyoming um to their to their little gathering. And why? He's all hard work. Um you think about the way he's kind of come up through college football, you know, following his career goes to Washington, then, you know, goes to Alabama and and he becomes really what was the top option for an Alabama team that made the college football playoff. I think he kind of gets it and that's why every time they put more on that guy's plate, he steps up. And he just continues to He knows the playbook inside and out. He's talking to Aaron Rodgers about route depth and how you want this route run. Do you want it run flatter? Do you want me to drift this way? There's so many different things about Jeremy Bernard that he understands about football. Um and that plays well with a guy like Rodgers who we know is so much about the peas and cues of a play on any given on any given down and he he will vocalize what he sees and what he wants. Um and that has been a really big motivating factor for Aaron, and you can tell he's just kind of cherishing these days with Mike McCarthy. Um but I don't think he's going to come back again, even if they're really good. I think it would have to be like I don't know. They'd have to go to like the AFC title game, and he would just have to like get this itch thinking, oh, one piece away from the Super Bowl. Um but man, he got beat up last year. I know he played most of the games. I think he played 16 of 17, only missed one with the wrist. But like he you can only take so much punishment at some point, man. And I do think Aaron at some point is going to walk away, want to want to kind of live out his days privately, but we'll see. I don't I don't think anyone has to worry about Drew Aller missing practice time. And obviously that is something that cannot happen. You know, he's he's a guy that has to still sign before Aller. It just doesn't make much sense for Aller to sign before Beck considering the structure of Beck's deal is going to directly affect what he gets. So I think it's a staring match here on when those guys sign. And when they do, I think eventually we will see him sign. Probably I would have guessed some point within the next week before training camp. I'd be pretty surprised if this drew into practice time. >> Good to know. Good to know. Um, you know, obviously the another comment about this offense and why the excitement is building heading into training camp is that you know, the reinforcement of the wide receiver room with bringing Pittman in and and now the one comment is basically saying you can't double anybody now with with DK, Pittman, and Bernard on the field assuming the rookie gets that kind of playing time because the other guy, Roman Wilson, could be a possibility. That is only behind the Bengals with $65.5 million, the Cowboys with $61.8 million, and the Lions at $52.6 million. So, a lot of money invested in a wide receiver room that was deficient after the trade of George Pickens a year ago. So, and we had talked about well, maybe some of these contracts like the DK Metcalf contract are aren't aging well. So, are they going to get the return on that investment? >> Well, you think about the other three you named and you think okay, it's Chasin Higgins, it's Olave and Pickens, it's Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. Like those are premier duos, you know, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, we'll see. You know, Metcalf has to have a less turbulent year than he did last year. I think that's one thing because he is the explosive playmaker on this When they when they look for explosiveness, he's going to be the guy they're going to turn to. Um, so they need him in a big way. I think Pittman's going to give them a dimension they just did not have last Um, the underneath chain mover that's steady-handed that can play inside or outside, that has really great hands, just the guy that can catch anything on third and five and make it a 7-yard game to keep to keep the chains moving, right? I They didn't have that really last year. Um, I think having him more and Pat Freiermuth out there more will help that. Um, so I think that will be a big thing. It It's kind of almost replacing Gainwell and Warren, you know, the dump off to the flats where they kind of just said throw it out to the flat and hope those two guys break tackles and get the first downs and they did. Um, you know, you can only do that for so long and doing it another year is probably not always going to work. So having someone like Pittman that can run a really diverse route tree and can do a lot of different things is really going to help. So I do think that there's definitely going to be a big-time step up in that production. And I think you have Jeremy Bernard who is really good after the catch. He's got great hands. He's a bigger-bodied guy, but he's kind of built like a running back in some ways. So you can get the screen game going to him. And if Roman Wilson took a step, I mean, that'd be huge for them to just have his speed out of the slot and his ability to kind of stretch the field vertically. Um, I'm not betting on that, obviously, but I think that would be a big-time step for them. But I do think they have the makings of a wide receiver room here that plays off each other really well. Metcalf, Pittman, Bernard kind of fill in their blank spots against one another and I think that can really be the sign of a healthy wide receiver room, especially for a guy like Aaron Rodgers. And Aaron Rodgers is just going to pick matchups out when with his mind. And having those different archetypes uh allows you to go against different DBs, different mentalities, different schemes, and attack them still. And I think that's a really important thing. >> No, I I I like it. And speaking of Rodgers' mind, there were certain plays when you're just watching him like when he you know, catches a guy trying to get off the field or something. He's just I would just love for 1 hour to see the game through Aaron Rodgers' eyes. Just just you know, I just can't imagine you know, blind and now I can see. I would just couldn't couldn't imagine like the football knowledge that that would come through by just being able to channel that brain of his. It is amazing. It it really is amazing. >> is. He is like boom boom boom snapshot. I mean, he sees it in a different way than most quarterbacks do. Um, he's seen every coverage in the book multiple times over. Uh, when when you're in the league as long as he is, you know that. Um, and he is someone that I mean, he can diagnose something at the line in 5 seconds. He understands it. You're not really fooling Aaron Rodgers. I I think Rodgers last year, you know, the Vikings defense had some struggles at times last year. I think when I was watching Rodgers he was one of the only quarterbacks, if not the only quarterback, I think that totally outsmarted Brian Flores' scheme. And we know that's a complex, hard-to-read scheme. It didn't work against Aaron Rodgers. He's seen everything at every point at every time. And so, really really fun to watch the mental side of his game. Even though, you know, the physical side, the arm's still there, the mobility sometimes hurts him and everything, but the mental side is so sharp. >> It's unbelievable. Just just fantastic to watch. Um, uh, we got a good vintage type of sentiment in the comments. We've been talking lots of offense. This guy wants to talk defense. He's high on Patrick Graham. He wants an old-style Steeler defense that's going to be scary to play. Intimidation, hitting, physicality. Are we going to see that with this 2026 Steelers D? >> Yeah, I mean I think PG absolutely has the type of mentality that fits into the historical lore, if you will. If you're you're looking for a real football guy, Patrick Graham is that. Very smart. Uh you just hear Patrick Graham speak and and Jean, I don't know if you watched Patrick Graham's interviews. I think we've talked to him about three or four times now. You could just see how smart he is. Obviously, he's Ivy League educated, so there's an expectation of that, but he kind of views football through a lens that I think is really fresh and new. Um there's a really holistic approach to that. Watching him on the practice field just kind of ramp through install is kind of crazy. This defense is like really well prepared. They're really honing in on communication. They're doing different things and already trying to disguise coverages and they're doing so much more than they were doing like this time last year defensively, just trying to go past installs. At this point, saying, "How can we install while still trying to diversify the scheme?" Um you know, disguise, do all these different things cuz we know Patrick Graham says there's no Patrick Graham scheme, so you got to have everything. Yeah, it's like a melting pot, right? There's a little bit of everything. You think about who he's worked for, Patrick Graham. Um you know, he's worked for Bill Belichick. He's worked for Brian Flores. He's worked for Pete Carroll. Um there's all these influence spheres that he has um that have combined into his defense and now he still has parts of Mike Tomlin's scheme and parts of Dick LeBeau's old Steelers scheme and even going all the way back to Dom Capers, right? There's just there's different kind of ingredients and finding the way it all fits together is really interesting. I do think they're going to be an attacking defense that's going to be downhill. They're going to blitz a good bit. I think they're going to be a split safety defense that plays a lot of cover two, cover six. Um I think you see that with the type of safeties they have with Brisker, Elliott, Ramsey, no true free safety on this roster. Absolutely is a hit there. They're going to play up in your face and press man on the outside. Dean and Porter have talked about that all spring. That is going to be something that they want to do. They want to get physical and they want to get up in your face. So, you better be able to get off press on the outside. And I do think they're going to be tricky. They're not going to, you know, just show you five and send five. They're going to drop out from different areas, bring the pressure from different areas. They're going to move guys around. No one's The picture is not going to be static. It's going to be different. I think it's going to be a fresh brand of defense. This does not all mean, just because there's all these changes, does not mean it's going to be good necessarily. But, you couldn't keep doing the same stuff when the deterioration was so stark last year, right? It was It just fell off a cliff. >> Right. >> The defense fell to 17th in scoring defense. They had the turnovers um still there, but they were living off kind of those those havoc plays and those turnovers rather than being a good defense down in and down out. I think Patrick Graham wants to find one thing and it's that. He wants to be a good team down in and down out. Um, and and we'll see if they can do that, but I definitely think the philosophy is going to be similar to some of the old school stuff where they're no, you know, hard-nosed and tough and trying to find their own way and just do his lord. >> No, we definitely want more scheme to the defense, but like you said, I wouldn't mind a little screaming from opposing offenses at the physicality that Pittsburgh in a new form brings to the table uh you with that old style heritage that we do have in Pittsburgh. He's nominating Roman Wilson, but we've seen so little from Roman Wilson of actual production during games. That is a real real head-scratcher because if you want to get this guy catching run opportunities in space, he's got to catch the ball and use his size and speed to do that. So, I I do think that is one thing. I do agree though, there is some thinness to this room. Roman needs to be someone that steps up because they don't have another guy that can really fill that deep deep threat void, but on top of that, they don't really necessarily have a true guy that plays outside. I mean, Bernard and Pittman are both types that probably are like Z slot types, but DK's like the only X. Um I I know that they're cross-training them all, but they're not prototypical in that area. Could Bernard do it, and then you could throw Roman in at the slot? Sure, but they need Roman Wilson, or they need to go out and acquire a an outside wide receiver. I mean, the one guy I've always pointed to if they wanted to acquire one was Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots. He started last year on the Super Bowl team on that Super Bowl team that lost to the Seahawks. Uh and he probably is on the way out because of the A.J. Brown trade. Um they just kind of have a glut there of of wide receivers, and you could probably have him for a day-three pick. I mean, that wouldn't be a bad idea if that's what you really needed. If DK gets hurt, they are probably in trouble. Um and they are in a real bind there with how thin that position is. That and safety. Two the two thinnest positions on this roster. If they get an injury to either of those spots, they're in a bad spot. So, I definitely would look to strengthen those spots, but it would be nice if the Steelers had their own internal solution and Rowan Wilson's breakout was real. >> Uh that would be so nice. That would be so nice. Now, with with uh the countdown to camp officially underway, officially under a week right now, uh we got we got to say something about Camp McCarthy. I mean, what's it going to be like? More importantly, uh where is this uh guy, McCarthy, this Pittsburgh guy whose family owned a bar? Where is he going to go for his after-hours refreshment among the watering holes of of Latrobe? I mean, we got to we got to stake this out. >> We do. Uh yeah, you know, he was a bartender at his dad's bar out in Greenfield. If you know, there used to be um a club, I believe, down in Station Square called Chauncey's that he used to uh bounce at as well. McCarthy has a lot of fun bar scene stories in Pittsburgh. I don't know, you know, Sharky's uh is always there. Does he fancy himself on some wings? Could go to Dino's. If you want some pizza, Joe & O's is there. There's a lot of good spots out there. If you you're looking for a more like dingy retro spot that seems like it's straight out of the '70s or '80s, the Touchdown Club exists. There's a lot of fun fun little uh spots out there in Latrobe. It's not a big town, it's a very small town. So, you know, you could even go down a little bit more to Ligonier if you wanted to. There's some really good spots out there. Um and kind of when you then weave into town, there's some little coffee shops there, but I bet Mike McCarthy he fancys himself a wing guy. That Dino's might be the pick uh for for Big Mike. >> All right, we will count on you to uh let us know where he ends up and and what type of wing uh that uh uh fits his appetite. That will be interesting. Uh but, you know, certainly it's not as star-studded uh, situation as some of the Tomlin camps where he would get, you know, a poison lead singer coming in and you know, you know what I mean. What do you think that that that the tone's going to be like in terms of all the hoopla surrounding, you know, the work on on on the practice field? >> I think it's going to be really interesting to see how Mike McCarthy reacts to Latrobe, because you think about a college campus open to the public, you think about like every NFL franchises or most of the NFL franchises uh, training camps nowadays and most of them are in the facility away from the public facing eye. Steelers meanwhile have embraced this community tradition that's been happening for now nearly 60 years, a little bit over 60 years, and have just run with it. Um, it's very unique and so I do think, you know, coming from Pittsburgh you kind of have stands that and and will embrace that part of it. So I have no doubt that he's going to make this a big thing for the fan base and lean into the Pittsburgh crowd and all of that. I do think there's going to be a lot of work, work, work. I think there's going to be um, a good deal of install still going on. They still have to get the scheme in fully. I think there's going to be more team periods this year. Maybe no seven shots, which is a sad thing cuz I love seven shots. Those are great. Um, those are great um, kind of physical period. I do think we're going to see backs on backers still here. I think we're going to see some of those physical things, but I don't think it's going to be as physical. Tomlin beat those guys down, man. I mean, he would put them in pads multiple times back-to-back. Sometimes they could only do it two days in a row generally speaking, but he would do it the maximum amount of that and they would hit. I mean, they would smoke each other. Um, and so I think that was always something with Tomlin that was like, you knew you were going through a really hard training camp. I can't remember how many times I I talked with with guys that said, Tomlin's training camps were the hardest training camps they ever went through because of [clears throat] just how much they hit and he had all the practices at you know, 2:00 in the afternoon, 3:00 in the afternoon, right when it was the hottest it would be in the day and you would just sweat and it it would really test your conditioning and your endurance and it was a slog, man. Um but McCarthy's feel like they're going to be less less of that, you know, you're going to wake up early, do your walk-through early in the morning, you're going to get your breakfast, you're going to come out for practice at get your, you know, lunch, then do some studying after that and then you kind of feels like the evening might be a little more free, you know, to maybe for the guys to go out and get a bite or whatever they might want to do, team bonding activity, what whatever they may want to do. So, it's going to be very interesting, but I do think the on-field stuff is going to be very much um a little more drawn back on the physicality, more on the instruction, more team periods and it's going to be more of a I I don't want to say instructional camp, but I would say somewhere around there. And to a degree almost militant at times, but Mike Tomlin's camps were notoriously extremely hard. So, uh we'll we'll see how McCarthy's measure up because Mike T didn't pull any punches. He would go a little easier during the season, um but man, training camps were always really hard with Mike T was around. >> Well, that will be a an interesting change and you know, to see the results as well, you know, to to see if this a different approach by McCarthy yields yields, you know, the results that we want to see, especially with this offense. Do you think Hindenburg or Wejan could be injected into the passing game and receive looks from Rodgers? I mean, you got tight ends, you got the trio receivers. Now you got you know these upstart guys that may want the ball as well. What do you think? >> Well, Hindenburg has to prove he deserves to be on the roster. We'll see. They keep four running backs and maybe cuz he proves his receiving ability plus his rushing ability really brings a different style to that that room than others. Obviously, he's a four-phase special teamer, returner, all these different things that he does. But if he can prove that, then sure. He can almost be like having a seventh receiver and a fourth running back, right? That's kind of the beauty of him if he can make it. But Wejan, I think is the interesting one because he lit up the Shrine Bowl from a receiver perspective. I think that's what put him really on the Steelers radar was his stand-up performance at the Shrine Bowl where he was just routing guys up, beating them out of the slot. He didn't do much at all in the receiving side of things at Iowa. It wasn't part of his game really, but could they give him screens, jet sweeps, things out of the backfield. I think he's a manufactured touch guy and I think that's what he is. He's electric in space. He's really quick. He's able to do one move after the other in succession because of his agility. He's slippery in space. I think it's really going to kind come down to how well they can maximize his skill set. We've seen Mike McCarthy utilize guys like Wejan before in his offenses where he'll just get the ball in their hands and kind of say go to work. I'm interested to see how electric he is with the ball in his hands cuz sometimes the return skills don't always translate onto offense either. You know, you can be a really great returner, it doesn't always mean you're great in space. So, we'll see how uh how Wejan is, but he's obviously a great returner. The question's now going to be how much of an offensive role can he take on, but I have no doubt he's going to get some manufactured touches. They They talked about that very heavily after they drafted him during draft weekend. And if Mike McCarthy I've learned something. If Mike McCarthy says something that seems pretty candid, he probably is being pretty candid. So, believe him a little bit there. I think that you're going to see Wejin take on some of those manufactured touches, for sure. >> A manufactured touch guy who is electric in space. You got to love to see it. Uh as speaking of love, you guys in the comments and in the audience, be back here next Tuesday right around 4:00 because that will be your chance to pick Nick's brain on the first day of training camp for the Pittsburgh Steelers. It all begins next Tuesday, and then it is a magic carpet ride, a run right through the season. And it's all going to be here every Tuesday right around 4:00, where we're taking your comments, and we're talking your favorite football team. Until then, go Steelers.

title: Aaron Donald's expected return to Rams may not be immediate | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: I want to start with the latest little breadcrumb on the trail that is going to lead Aaron Donald back to the National Football League. Schefter made the comment on his podcast that Donald may not be back in the immediate future. That Donald is in the process of getting himself back into football shape. Which is fine. But it means he's coming back. That's the headline. If he's taking time to get himself into football shape, he's coming back to play football. It reminds me the old Jerry Seinfeld bit where he said all these people are trying to get into shape. What are you trying to get into shape for? You're just trying to get into shape for what? Well, Aaron Donald isn't trying to get into football shape so he can declare to the world on social media, "I'm in football shape." He's getting himself into football shape so he can play football. And no, they don't need him right out of the gates. He may have no desire to go to Australia for the week one game. This is about having him ready when they need him. They don't need him week one, week two. They don't really based upon the quality of the team. Now, at some point he's got to get comfortable with them. They've got to get comfortable with him. I pointed out recently how dramatically the roster has changed since he retired after the 2023 season. There's only one defensive starter who was there when Donald last played. That's linebacker Byron Young. So, you do need a break-in period. the final assault to the Super Bowl mountain, at least to the summit, begins week 15 when they play the Seahawks for the first time. They don't need Donald until then. They don't need him to be at 100% firing on all cylinders, being the guy who can beat single teams handily and get to the quarterback or otherwise just blow up the play, F the play up as Sims would say. With Myles Garrett getting extra attention, that's the thing, Aaron Donald doesn't have to come back and be the guy Aaron Donald was. There's a percentage less than what he used to be where he's still going to be as dominant, if not more dominant, because you can't devote the resources to stopping him like he used to. Why did he retire? He got burned out. It's easy to get burned out when every time you line up, you got two or three guys trying to keep you from doing your job. It gets old. Now, maybe that won't happen. That had to be the thing that caused him to explore whether or not he can light the fire again. So, if it takes a while to get the fire started and then you've got the kindling, you've got you know, the whole process before it's fully engulfed, if that takes a few weeks or longer into the regular season, so be it. This isn't about trotting out Aaron Donald when they introduce the starting lineups in Melbourne. This is about Aaron Donald being in the starting lineup when they play the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium in February of 2027. okay, fine. He may not be back in the immediate future. But the way it's presented, sure looks like he's coming back. And when he does, the Rams will be the presumptive Super Bowl champions. They're already the favorites. That continues to be the biggest challenge. And Dan Patrick and I were about this the other day on his show, "I'll take it." as Dan said. And yes, it's great to have a team that is perceived to be stocked and the clear favorite to win the Super Bowl. But, still got to motivate your players. And when they start reading what everyone is writing, hearing what everyone is saying, dealing with the fact that every game is going to be the Super Bowl for every team that plays them. And then you throw in injuries. That one thing that we know will happen, but we don't know who it will happen to or when. It's the unpredictable reality of playing the games that will tend to turn favorites into also-rans. And if a team stays healthy, it otherwise wouldn't supposed to be competitive. Well, if everyone else has injury issues and they stay healthy, that team ends up being a contender. Keeping your key players healthy for as long as possible is one of the core ingredients in emerging as a true contender at the end of the season. So, one way to keep Aaron Donald healthy is to not play him until you need him. And it sounds like that's the direction where that is going. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube. title: Matthew Berry’s Best Advice for Auction League Fantasy Drafting | The Rich Eisen Show
text: Our league is actually auction, Matt, you know, so we don't do the the serpentine. So it's like you're dealing with a budget here. The big position, like you said earlier, running back. And we know the names at the top of the list. So tell me, for the people who are in auction leagues, who would you bid the most money on? Who Who would you spend the most money on the running back position? >> I mean, look, you know, all the all the obvious names are right there. Look, I have Bijan, I have Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson right there at 1 2 just like everyone. So those are the two running that should go for the most money. But here's what I'll say just in general when you're doing a salary cap league, or as you call it TJ, an auction league, when you're doing something like that, I'm a big believer in as we just talked about with Brockman, like get your guys. Here's my Here's my strategy there. Too many times I've been in the those kind of drafts where people are like, "Oh, you know, gosh, I I really want I really want Carnell Tate." So they're sitting [clears throat] there and they're like, "I'm going to hold on to Carnell Tate. I'm going to hold on to And then you get to And then all these big name wide receivers go. And then you get to Carnell Tate and you're like, "I've got a mark up for like I think he's a $20 player." And then like but you get there and there's three other guys that love Carnell Tate and he's like the last wide receiver two guy lot left and all of a sudden he's going for $35. So I'm a big I'm a big believer I'm a big believer and if there's a guy that you want in that type of draft, throw him out there. So like I used Jeremiah Love earlier. Let's say you you want Jeremiah Love and you've got him listed at Again, it depends on your salary cap and your scoring system and how many teams, but let's call him a a $45 player just for just for a number. So he's a $45 player. And so you've marked out that I'm I'm willing to go to $50 for Jeremiah Love cuz I really believe in him this year. I love him. Well, I want to throw him out early because I want to know either do I get Jeremiah Love for, you know, $50 or less. But in a world where there's a bidding war and there's three other great fans of of Jeremiah and he goes for like 55 or $60 cuz people at the beginning of those kind of drafts tend to spend a lot of money, then you can at least pivot as opposed to, you let Saquon go by and he he goes for less than he should cuz people are out on Saquon this year or James Cook or some of these other, you know, running backs that have been around for a little bit longer. And um and then you're so you're missing out on the bargains and then it gets to the player you want and you get outbid because there's three or four other teams that have too much money left. So, I'm a big believer in throwing out the player you want early so you know whether you've got him or if you have to pivot. Um the last thing I will say about a league like that is it's very important to understand where the value has come. Sometimes they come early in the draft cuz everyone's holding on to their money.
